runs.text: Introduce Roam as an academic web development project. The system serves travelers and administrators. Explain that package bookings and payments are demonstrations, while personal planning records persist in the database.
One place for the whole trip
Destination ideas, schedules and expense notes can become difficult to manage separately.
A personal workspace that keeps each trip connected to its itinerary, budget, packing and memories.
Planning tools + database persistence + administrator control
Describe the problem as the project motivation, rather than a measured research finding. The objective is to demonstrate a complete database-backed travel workflow.

Discover destinations, create personal plans and request demo packages.
Curate the catalog, maintain suppliers and manage bookings and access.
Server-side permissions protect every role-specific action.
After sign-in, travelers enter their personal dashboard. Administrators land in the Operations overview with separate navigation. Server-side permission checks enforce the distinction.

This is the coverage overview. The following slides explain every original traveler menu area, the package extension and the administration workspace.

Registration depends on the administrator setting. Profile includes trip history and wishlist. Logout can be cancelled. Do not display real credentials during the classroom demonstration.

Browse by destination, trip type or season.

Season browsing covers Summer, Monsoon, Autumn and Winter. Each season has a distinct hover or keyboard-focus animation, respecting reduced-motion preferences. Season suitability is curated, and prices are sample estimates. Image is an illustrative bundled asset, not a destination guarantee.

Per-person estimates exclude travel to the destination.

This is a transparent rule-based algorithm, not a trained AI model. Cost equals daily destination estimate multiplied by the selected number of days, per person. Interests use case-insensitive activity-text matching. The maximum is 100 points. Estimates exclude travel to the destination.

Compare rates, season, duration, attractions and activities before choosing.
Comparison lasts for the browser session. Wishlist saves persist.
Comparison selections last only for the browser session. Wishlist records persist in the database for the current account. These features support choosing a destination before committing to a plan.

Suggested activities or a blank itinerary.
A group budget and an editable seasonal packing list.

Explain a transaction: related records succeed together or roll back together if something fails. The generated lists are starting points that travelers can edit. Destination estimates are per person, while entered trip budgets are group totals.

Add activities, update details and remove entries.
Print the schedule or save as PDF.
Cancel or complete a trip. Finished trips lock editing.

Cancelled and completed trips become read-only. Shortening a trip is rejected if itinerary entries lie beyond the proposed final day. Changing destinations preserves manually edited itinerary and packing contents, so users should review them afterward. PDF output uses the browser print function.

A clear view of the group budget
With INR 18,500 in estimates, the group can adjust spending before travel.
Add, edit and remove estimates. All entered amounts are group totals.

Illustrative classroom example: a group budget of INR 20,000 with expenses totaling INR 18,500 leaves INR 1,500. This is an example, not a real quote. Server-side money calculations use decimal values.
Illustrative amounts are presentation examples, not live quotes. Example sum: 18,500, budget 20,000, remaining 1,500. Source: docs/FEATURES.md.
Add custom items and save checked progress.
Days, hours, minutes and seconds until the next eligible trip.
Checked packing items persist in the database. The countdown follows local device dates and is a planning aid. It chooses the earliest eligible planned trip.

For completed trips: upload a photo with a title, trip date and personal note.
One 1–5 review per completed trip. Read the administrator’s reply in your account.

Memory dates must fall within the trip. Travelers can delete their memories. Photo retrieval checks ownership, and uploads are decoded and re-encoded with metadata removed. Feedback prevents multiple reviews for the same trip.

Per-person INR price, duration, traveler limit and daily itinerary.
Inclusions, exclusions and cancellation rules are visible before a demo request.
Clients see published packages with active destinations and suppliers.
A package appears to clients only if it is published and its destination, hotel and transportation are active. Personal trip planning and package bookings are separate workflows.

Bookings and payments are a demo
Choose package dates and traveler count.
My bookings shows requests and payment history.
Receipts and refunds calculate unpaid, partial and paid states.
No money moves. No hotel or transport reservation occurs.

Make the simulation boundary explicit when presenting. Simulate full payment records only a demonstration receipt. The server calculates totals, preserves booking snapshots and blocks excessive receipts or refunds. No payment gateway is connected.

Edit region, description, season, category, cost, activities and imagery. Publish or hide.
Maintain address, room details and amenities. Archive and restore supplier records.
Maintain modes, routes and service details, including mixed journeys.
Hidden catalog entries retain links to previous trips and bookings.

Historical trips retain destination references when entries are hidden. Published packages must first be unpublished before associated hotel or transport records can be archived. Administrators can represent a mixed transport journey.
Website screenshots show demonstration data. Bundled photograph provenance: docs/ASSETS.md.
Link suppliers, set pricing and terms, then save Draft or Published.
Confirm, cancel or complete eligible bookings.
Record demo receipts/refunds and preserve original booking details.

Completion requires the booking end date to have passed. Deleting a package removes its catalog listing while preserving historical bookings. Frozen package and supplier details retain what the customer originally requested. Payment status comes from ledger amounts rather than an editable label.

Enable or disable travelers. Revoked access invalidates existing sessions.
Control registrations, the dashboard announcement and support email.
Read feedback and send a response visible to the traveler.
Review user/trip totals, average ratings and recent administrator audit events.

Disabling an account invalidates its sessions. Administrator accounts have safeguards against accidental lockout through client controls. User and feedback lists paginate, and role validation protects each admin API route.

Explain the purpose of each layer. Bootstrap supports styling. JavaScript handles browser interactions and JSON requests. Servlets process requests. Services implement rules. JDBC accesses the relational database. The production WAR uses MySQL, while the default local launcher uses H2.
Website screenshots show demonstration data. Bundled photograph provenance: docs/ASSETS.md.
A request through the MVC layers
Runs JDBC work and stores sessions

Request journey: the browser sends a same-origin JSON request, ApiController checks session, role and CSRF, the service validates and performs database work, then JSON returns for the browser to render. MVC keeps display, request handling and business logic separate.
Website screenshots show demonstration data. Bundled photograph provenance: docs/ASSETS.md.
Supporting tables store settings, audit events, login attempts and sessions.

Additional infrastructure tables hold settings, audit events, login attempts, schema versions and web sessions. Relational links support ownership checks and durable history. Memory and feedback operations depend on completed trips.
Website screenshots show demonstration data. Bundled photograph provenance: docs/ASSETS.md.
Salted PBKDF2 passwords, timed sessions and current account checks.
Ownership checks restrict trips, photos and bookings to their users.
CSRF tokens, prepared SQL, escaped HTML and rate limits.
Validate image size, normalize photos and remove metadata.

Passwords use PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 with 600,000 iterations and unique salts. Session IDs rotate after login. Cookies use HttpOnly and SameSite, with Secure under HTTPS deployment. Session expiry is 30 minutes. HTML escaping and a Content Security Policy also protect rendering. These controls reduce risk but do not imply security certification.
Website screenshots show demonstration data. Bundled photograph provenance: docs/ASSETS.md.
Recorded repository results cover trip, security and package workflows.

These are recorded results from the repository maintenance verification, not tests rerun for this presentation. Package tests cover draft visibility, stale versions, party limits, duplicate requests, ownership, frozen booking data, partial/full/refunded amounts and history preservation. Local results do not establish hosted performance.

Start the server, sign in and explore a destination.
Show itinerary changes, group budget and packing progress.
Explain package requests, simulated payments and catalog controls.

Run start-local.cmd, then open http://127.0.0.1:8080 while the server is running. Prepare separate demo traveler and administrator accounts beforehand. Use a completed sample trip to demonstrate memories and feedback. Avoid changing real user records during the demonstration.
Website screenshots show demonstration data. Bundled photograph provenance: docs/ASSETS.md.
What works now. What comes next.
Personal planning with database storage, role-based administration and demo package bookings.
Real reservations and verified payments, live prices/weather and email notifications.
Hosted performance checks, accessibility review and provider integration.

Destination estimates and season suitability are sample/curated content. No live travel provider, real payment gateway or email delivery currently works. Real payments would require signed provider webhooks, transaction identifiers and server-side reconciliation. Hosting configuration does not itself prove a production deployment. Future items are proposals.
Website screenshots show demonstration data. Bundled photograph provenance: docs/ASSETS.md.

Closing talking points: Roam demonstrates a complete Java MVC application with relational persistence, two roles, editable planning records and transactional workflows. Be ready to explain rule-based recommendations, group budgets versus per-person prices, booking snapshots and simulated payments.
